components.source_check: Durrett p. 244: the definition lim_M sup_i E(|X_i|;|X_i|>M)=0, the remark sup_i E|X_i| <= M+1 (annex lines 6-7) and the dominated example (body lines 43-44) are all present. The entry restricts the definition to integrable families; by the source's own M+1 remark every family uniformly integrable in the source's sense is integrable, so the class is unchanged. Small-event control, the empty-family convention and the E(Z;A) notation are added and stated.

Durrett p. 244 (dominated example; the epsilon-delta property used in the proof of Theorem 4.6.1). Both directions of the equivalence, the dominated and finite-family cases and the bounded-first-moment counterexample are each proved in the annex.

Durrett Theorem 4.6.2, p. 245: phi >= 0 with phi(x)/x -> infinity, examples x^p (p>1) and x log^+ x, E phi(|X_i|) <= C implies uniform integrability; all preserved (Borel measurability is the condition under which the source's E phi(|X_i|) is defined). The added convex converse is stated and fully proved.

Durrett Theorem 4.6.1, p. 244: the family {E(X|F): F a sigma-field in F_o} is uniformly integrable; the source's point that such families can be very large is carried by body lines 69-71. Proof written (Markov bound, |E(X|G)| <= E(|X| |G), defining identity on the G-event).

Durrett Lemma 4.6.5, p. 246 (item 5, strengthened to uniformity over A) and the tools the source's proofs invoke (L1 implies in probability; bounded convergence in probability; Fatou in probability form); each of the five items is proved in the annex.

Durrett Theorem 4.6.3, pp. 245-246: hypotheses E|X_n| < infinity and X_n -> X in probability; the three equivalent conditions; the clipping map phi_M for (i)=>(ii), the Jensen step for (ii)=>(iii) and the cutoff psi_M (x on [0,M-1], 0 on [M,inf), linear between) with the finitely-many-early-terms step for (iii)=>(i). All retained and written.

Durrett Theorem 4.6.4, p. 246: the three equivalent conditions for a submartingale and the proof via the martingale convergence theorem and Theorem 4.6.3. The added supermartingale form, F_infinity-measurable limit and X_n <= E(X_infinity|F_n) are proved (annex lines 204-222).
Durrett Theorem 4.6.7(iv), p. 247: an integrable X with X_n = E(X|F_n); the entry also states that the closing variable need not be F_infinity-measurable, which thm:p15-closed-martingale works out.

Durrett Lemmas 4.6.5-4.6.6, p. 246 and Theorem 4.6.7, p. 247: all four conditions, the (iii)=>(iv) identity X_n = E(X|F_n) and (iv)=>(i) through Theorem 4.6.1; the added identification X_infinity = E(Z|F_infinity) is proved by the pi-lambda argument.

Durrett Theorem 4.6.8, p. 247: F_n increasing to F_infinity = sigma(union F_n), E(X|F_n) -> E(X|F_infinity) a.s. and in L1; the source's proof (tower, Theorem 4.6.1, Theorem 4.6.7, Lemma 4.6.6, pi-lambda identification) is written in full, with the measurable limit off the convergence event.

Durrett Theorem 4.6.9 (Levy's 0-1 law) and its continuation, pp. 247-248. Present: the statement (with an added L1 mode), the 'immediate consequence' proof from the upward theorem, and the Kolmogorov tail zero-one law argument (annex lines 293-303). Absent from the route: the source's discussion of the theorem's meaning.
components.gap: Preserve the identified source variants of Durrett's Theorem 4.6.9 and its continuation (pp. 247-248): the route supplies the statement, its proof and the tail zero-one consequence, but not the source's justificatory discussion that follows the theorem - Chung's challenge to the reader to judge whether the result is obvious or incredible; the 'obvious' reading (1_A is F_infinity-measurable and F_n increases to F_infinity, so the best guess of 1_A given F_n should approach the best guess given F_infinity, which is 1_A); the presentation of the Kolmogorov zero-one law consequence as the 'incredible' reading; and Durrett's evaluation that this argument may not show the theorem to be too improbable to be possible, but that it and the later applications (Exercises 4.6.4-4.6.5) show it is a very useful result. Only the formal steps behind the two readings appear (annex lines 289-303). Durrett Example 4.6.11, p. 248: X_n = Y_n Z_n with independent P(Y_n=1)=1/n, P(Z_n=n)=1/n (here n B_n C_n), X_n -> 0 a.s. and uniformly integrable, F = sigma(Y_1,Y_2,...), E(X_n|F) = Y_n converging in L1 but not a.s.: complete construction and every step proved. Items 1-2 are added boundary examples, each proved.
